claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: The pinned family-332 manuscript states that real sequence ell_1 has metric Markov cotype two constant N_2 <= 12*sqrt(21) (squared constant 3024). Its definition assumes a finite state space, t>=1, a reversible stochastic matrix and stationary probability vector; the proof's Remark 5.1 says stationarity alone suffices.
claims.status: source_reported; internally reconstructed and independently source-audited; not externally referee or proof-assistant validated
claims.proof_path: METRIC_EXTENSION_STRONGER.md, section 'Exact release claim and proof mechanism'; source extraction at children/metric_representation/sources/l1-markov-cotype-extracted.txt
claims.novelty_boundary: The theorem is a pinned OpenAI release claim, not a result independently established by this lane. Naor v2 added-in-proof reports forthcoming Mendel-Naor work proving metric Markov cotype 2 for L1[0,1], so no qualitative novelty claim is made.
claims.costs: The proof is finite-dimensional but uses up to 2^n-2 cut coordinates in its general statement. The explicit median constructor reduces to at most m(n-1) feature-threshold cuts for supplied n-by-m vectors.
claims.falsifier: A finite rational chain/data counterexample violating the exact 3024 inequality for the stated constructed points, or a proof gap in the quartic estimate, stopped-walk identity, or endpoint conversion.
claims.next_gate: Obtain external specialist review or formal verification of the family-332 proof; acquire and compare the full MN26 manuscript.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: Conditional on MR-RELEASE-COTYPE-L1, every finite family in any real ambient L1(Omega,mu) admits the same cotype-2 inequality with constant 12*sqrt(21). Pointwise finite threshold gaps give an exact weighted cut code and a contractive affine recovery map into the given ambient L1.
claims.novelty_boundary: No qualitative cotype novelty is claimed. Naor v2 added-in-proof reports forthcoming cotype-2 work for Lebesgue L1[0,1]; arbitrary-measure transfer is a direct finite-cut consequence, not a priority-cleared result.
claims.costs: Requires actual measurable representatives and finite lattice operations/integrals; the theorem provides existence, not arbitrary-L1 input computation.
claims.falsifier: A finite family whose pointwise integrated cut gaps fail the pairwise L1 identity or contractive recovery identity.
claims.next_gate: Compare exact scope and constants with MN26 when its full text is accessible.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: Conditional on the released ell_1 cotype theorem and Mendel-Naor Corollary 1.13, if X has finite Markov type-2 constant M_2(X), every Lipschitz map from any subset S of X into any real ambient L1 extends globally with Lip(F)<=C_MN*12*sqrt(21)*M_2(X)*Lip(f). The proof handles arbitrary range and nonseparable X by finite-data extensions into L1**, product weak-star compactness, and the norm-one L-projection from L1** onto L1.
claims.status: internally reconstructed conditional existence theorem; nonconstructive
claims.proof_path: METRIC_EXTENSION_STRONGER.md, sections 'Nonseparable finite-to-global bridge' and 'Prior art and novelty boundary'
claims.novelty_boundary: Qualitative L1 cotype and resulting linear-M_2 extension are author-source-reported forthcoming MN26 claims for L1[0,1]; this is not asserted as a new qualitative extension theorem. C_MN is unspecified, and the MN26 full proof was unavailable.
claims.costs: Existence only. The extension corollary factor is unspecified; product compactness and L-embedded projection give no runtime, bit complexity, or computable selector.
claims.falsifier: A defect in finite-code recovery, the dual-target extension interface, the L-embedded L-projection premise, or the finite-intersection argument.
claims.next_gate: Externally review the premise and compare MN26's quantitative source theorem; do not claim constructive global extension.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For rational row-stochastic A in Q^(n by n), integer t>=1 and rational vectors x_i in Q^m, compute G=((t+1)I-tA)^(-1) and y_i=E med(x_J1,x_J2,x_J3) for independent J_a distributed as row G_i. Sorted value thresholds compute every y_i exactly with O(n^3+mn^2+mn log n) rational arithmetic operations and polynomial bit complexity. Conditional on the family-332 proof and stationary pi, this is its finite-data cotype witness with the 3024 bound.
claims.status: mathematically derived exact constructor; reference implementation and finite differential tests; universal cotype guarantee conditional on source proof
claims.novelty_boundary: The expected-median identity is already family-332 Remark 5.3. The threshold implementation and bit-cost analysis are a reusable implementation consequence, not a novelty claim; no comparison with unpublished MN26 code was possible.
claims.costs: Full explicit rational A and n-by-m data are supplied. Output rational bit lengths are polynomial; a transition-sampler alternative costs three geometric paths, 3t expected transition calls per state, and returns a randomized sample rather than exact expectation.
claims.falsifier: Differential mismatch with exact triple enumeration or a rational stationary test instance violating the exact finite inequality.
claims.next_gate: Independent code/proof review, optimized exact arithmetic benchmark, and comparison with the full MN26 construction.

claims.status: internally proved model-scoped information-theoretic counterexample; novelty unverified

claims.costs: Precision threshold is b<=0.5 log2(d)-log2(a); unlimited additional queries do not distinguish the pair under the adversarial model.
claims.falsifier: A transcript-based algorithm distinguishes the pair under a shared admissible oracle, or an error is found in the exact TV separation proof.
claims.next_gate: Analyze round-to-nearest, dithered stochastic, and value-plus-gradient interfaces separately.
